newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMut says supports end of "six pillars".
newsitem.headline: NatMut says supports end of "six pillars".

text.p: Life insurance group National Mutual Ltd said on Wednesday it saw no immediate effect on it stemming from the Australian government's scrapping of the "six pillars" policy in the wake of the Wallis report.
"We support the Treasurer's decision to abolish the 'six pillars' policy, although we do not envisage this having an immediate impact on National Mutual," the company said in a statement.
The Wallis inquiry recommended that the policy, which prevented mergers among the four biggest banks and two largest life companies, should be removed.
Treasurer Peter Costello said the government had decided to end the "six pillars" policy, but ruled out mergers between the big four banks at present.
National Mutual has said it is not interested in buying an Australian bank, despite its ongoing push into the Australian home lending market which is dominated by banks.

National Mutual said it strongly endorsed the recommendation that a new prudential agency, the Corporations and Financial Services Commission (CSFC), be established to provide Commonwealth regulation of corporations, financial market integrity and consumer protection.
National Mutual is 51 percent owned by French insurance giant AXA SA.
